_readme: The shape every client portal starts as. Copy to data/clients/<slug>.json,
replace anything in ANGLE BRACKETS, delete cards the project does not have,
then push it to Blobs, which is the copy clients actually read:
Written 2026-08-25 after CBC's portal was built by hand and drifted out of
date four separate ways in eleven days. Every card here exists because a
real client needed it, and the wording is taken from portals that worked.
Two rules that are not optional:
1. A card item is a PROMISE TO THE CLIENT. If it says we need something
from them, it must stop saying that the moment they send it. See
2. checklist is a list of things we still need. Delete it from any item
marked complete, or the item contradicts itself on the page.
Also add the client to data/clients-index.json and set their passcode env
var, PORTAL_PASSWORD_<NAME>, in the PRODUCTION context. A portal with no
passcode set looks finished and lets nobody in. CBC's sat like that for ten
days with the passcode already emailed to five people.
name: <Client Legal Name>

cards.label: Discovery
cards.description: What we learned about your business, and what you told us you need.

cards.label: Proposal
cards.description: What we are building, what it costs, and how long it takes.

cards.label: Contract
cards.description: Your agreement is ready. Open it, read it through, and the Sign button is on the document itself. Anything you want changed, just say.

items.title: Your agreement
items.description: The full text, exactly as you will sign it. The Sign button is on the document.

items.title: Sign the contract
items.description: Your details are already filled in. You add your business address, then sign. Michelle countersigns after you and your signed copy comes back here.

cards.label: Payments
cards.description: $<DEPOSIT> is due on signing, before work begins. The remaining $<BALANCE> is due at launch. Hosting is included and there is no recurring cost to us.
cards._description_rule: ONE amount at a time, never the project total. Michelle 2026-08-20 on an invoice showing the whole ledger: it looks like he needs to pay me 2000 again.

items.title: How to pay
items.content:
Zelle is simplest and costs you nothing extra. Send to 908 906 1745 and put <MS-2026-XXX> in the memo so we can match it to your invoice.

Card, if that is easier. The processor charges 2.99% plus $0.49, which is their fee rather than ours, and it is the only reason Zelle is cheaper.
items._fee_rule: 2.99% + $0.49 is PayPal's real published US rate. It is NOT 4%. That wrong number was live on CBC's portal and in the invoice template until 2026-08-25.

cards.label: Onboarding
cards._locked_rule: Unlocks when the deposit clears. Nobody starts onboarding for free.
cards.description: What we need from you to get started.

items.title: Accounts to set up, all in your name
items.content: These are created in your name, not ours, so you own every one of them and could hand this to any developer later.

cards.label: Deliverables
cards.description: Everything we are building, and where each piece is up to.

cards.label: Offboarding
cards.description: Handover. Passwords, documentation, and a recorded walkthrough so your team can run this without us.

cards.label: Meeting Notes
cards.description: What we agreed, each time we spoke.

_workingNotes_readme: How this client works with us. Internal: the portal renderer never
touches this key, so none of it reaches the page. Write it as though
they will read it anyway. Operational facts in neutral language, never
a judgment about a person, what they are willing to pay, or how
Filled from three places, in this order: the working-preference
question in the Discovery Intake, what Michelle says about them, and
the mail record itself. Every field is optional and an empty block
ideaBacklog state is evidence, not intention. delivered means the
thing exists and we can point at it. quoted means a real number went
to them in writing. discussed means it was raised and nothing was
promised. Everything else is not started.
